title: Push and pull
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Do you chase journalists or do they come to you?
Jose said that chapter 11 is about push and pull. Pushing is when you have a story and push it into a media channel, and it is much harder: you tell a journalist, I really want you to publish this.
He said to put your publicist's details when you publish, and not your own name.
Jose said you want to go to a channel that is interested in what you do as a professional, and not sell them something. You want coverage on your expertise.
A student said that the longer route is to speak at events so your name gains traction and people come to you.
Another said: a writer or editor needs content. If you write an article up to their standards, you are not talking about your brand or endorsing it, you are writing news.
Jose said: show you understand the type of articles they write and their audience, and that you know their value proposition.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write three outlets that fit your expertise.
Write the article they would want.
Write the event where you could speak first.
Write what you will not say about your brand.

check.q: What did Jose say pushing is?
choices: Pushing your story into a channel

check.q: What did a student say an editor needs?
What did Jose say to show an editor?

recap: Pull, do not push. Write what the editor needs.
